correctness.rationale: For every even d=2m>=4 and Q=2^d, Witt extension makes one column uniform among Q-1 nonzero vectors and a distinct-column pair uniform on independent (x,y) with fixed symplectic pairing c=0/1; orbit sizes (Q-1)(Q/2-2) and (Q-1)Q/2. Character orthogonality and removal of x=0,y=0,x=y yield exactly β, (Q+4)/((Q-1)(Q-4)) and 1/(Q-1) pair correlations. These produce G_coord=(1-β)I+β(J⊗J)+a(K⊗K)+b(M⊗M). Matching involution decomposition U⊕V⊕W has dims 1,m-1,m and simultaneous eigenvalue triples (d,1,d-2),(0,1,-2),(0,-1,0). Tensor modes and the 2x2 constant/uniform block yield spectrum s[2(m-1)],t[2m²],r[(m-1)²],v[m²],ell±[1 each]. s=(Q²+(6-4d)Q-8)/((Q-1)(Q-4))>0 using 2^d>=4d. Exact determinant polynomials give s<ell-, and the maximum r for d=4,6 versus ell+ for d>=8; d=4 and d=6 are checked directly, and for d>=8 the polynomial signs are immediate from positive coefficients. Expansion gives kappa²=1+(d²+O(d))/2^d. Independent generation of all 720 Sp(4,2) elements matched all 289 exact Gram entries; a second independent script checked 18 representative pair correlations in dimensions 4,6,8, both symbolic determinant identities and 128 even-dimension sign instances. These finite checks corroborate rather than prove the universal case. The submitted code was inspected but not used as a substitute for proof.

value.rationale: The standard coordinate Walsh band restricted to uniform symplectic matrices is a natural stable-sampling/finite-group Fourier question: imposing the symplectic constraint breaks ordinary GL rank invariance into paired versus nonpaired coordinate orbits. The complete sharp Gram spectrum, equality-mode subspaces and strict m=4 crossover solve an all-rank conditioning problem whose answer cannot be read off a generic frame theorem or small table. This is a motivated and quantitatively exact spectral classification, not merely renaming a familiar frame or enumerating arbitrary instances. No claim is made of reconstruction of all group functions, higher Walsh degrees, or a new symplectic Fourier theory.

limitations: Restriction to standard symplectic basis, F2, m>=2, constant plus single-entry Walsh characters; no d=2, odd-field, higher-band or full-group Fourier result.
